topic: Nanbeige 4.3 33B: trending on Hugging Face, but will it fit your RAM?
thesis: Nanbeige4.3-33B trending is not the real story for you; the story is your RAM bank, because at Q4_K_M the download is 19.36 GiB and a 24 GB GPU holds it only with a sliver of the 524,288-token context on the card.
explanation_path: Start with the event the viewer saw: a 33B model from the Nanbeige team sitting fourth on Hugging Face trending two days after its repo went public, which earns it attention but says nothing about the machine under the desk. Establish what it is before judging it: a dense model in the ordinary LlamaForCausalLM layout, apache-2.0, built as the teacher for a family of smaller models, with vendor-reported scores that beat Qwen3.8-27B on Terminal-Bench 2.12 and lose to it on SWE-Bench Pro3. Then pivot from whether it is good to whether it fits, which is a question with exact answers: the original BF16 upload is 66237954048 bytes (61.69 GiB), but almost nobody downloads that; the file a local runner wants is a Q4_K_M GGUF at 20788825216 bytes (19.36 GiB). Before the viewer can weigh their own hardware, the second cost has to land: the KV cache, memory the model spends on context, which is 26.0 GiB at 128K in FP16 and about 104 GiB at the full 512K, on top of the weights. With both bills on the table the verdict sorts itself by machine: a 24 GB GPU runs it as 4-bit with roughly 8K-16K tokens of context, a 32 GB card buys a bigger quant, a 64 GB Mac or a 128 GB machine buys serious context. Land on what to do tonight: grab the GGUF and load it in LM Studio or Ollama via hf.co, since no official Ollama tag exists yet, and hold the honest catch to the end: vendor benchmarks, day-one conversions, and no measured tokens per second anywhere.

claims.claim: Nanbeige4.3-33B went public on 2026-10-24T02:49:18.000Z under the apache-2.0 license, published by the Nanbeige team as the flagship teacher model of the 4.3 series.

It is a dense model in the standard LlamaForCausalLM layout: 52 hidden layers, 56 attention heads, 8 key-value heads and a 166,912-entry vocabulary, with no mixture-of-experts keys anywhere in config.json.
The model card claims a context length of up to 524,288 tokens (512K).
On 2026-10-26 the model ranked fourth on Hugging Face's list of models sorted by trendingScore, showing 513 likes and 2,787 downloads.
claims.source_title: Hugging Face models API sorted by trendingScore (top 15)

claims.claim: The file that matters for local use, bartowski's Q4_K_M GGUF, is 20788825216 bytes (19.36 GiB); that conversion repo appeared 2026-10-25T14:22:25.000Z and already shows 18595 downloads.
The original BF16 weights the Nanbeige team uploaded total 66237954048 bytes (61.69 GiB) across 14 safetensors shards, roughly 3.2x the Q4_K_M file.
The context bill is separate from the weights: at 128K context an FP16 KV cache costs 26.0 GiB, and the full 512K context needs about 104 GiB for the cache alone.
claims.source_title: Nanbeige4.3-33B on a 24 GB GPU: Memory Math and Local Setup (webdiga)

claims.claim: A 24 GB GPU can run Nanbeige4.3-33B, but only as a 4-bit GGUF with roughly 8K-16K tokens of context, per an analysis built from the config and real quant file sizes rather than a measured run.
claims.source_title: Nanbeige4.3-33B on a 24 GB GPU: Memory Math and Local Setup (webdiga)

claims.claim: Ollama has no Nanbeige4.3-33B tag as of 2026-10-26: searching nanbeige on ollama.com returns 19 models and the newest is a Nanbeige4.2-3B upload from about 3 months ago.

Nanbeige's own table reports Nanbeige4.3-33B at 80.9 on Terminal-Bench 2.12 against 73.0 for Qwen3.8-27B, while Qwen3.8-27B leads SWE-Bench Pro3 at 61.7 to 60.3 and Gemma4-31B leads GPQA Diamond at 91.3.

analogy_candidates.mapping: The BF16 original is the 61.69 GiB hardcover set; the Q4_K_M GGUF is the same book reprinted smaller at 19.36 GiB so it fits the shelf you actually own, and the shelf is your RAM.
analogy_candidates.limit: Printing shrinks pages without losing words, while quantization does lose precision, and the shelf must still hold the growing bookmark pile: the KV cache.

analogy_candidates.mapping: Weights are furniture you carry in once; the KV cache is floor space for every guest, and each token of context is a guest, so a 512K party needs about 104 GiB of floor before anyone dances.
analogy_candidates.limit: Furniture is a fixed cost, but the cache can be booked at a cheaper rate: a q8_0 KV cache roughly halves the floor space, and furniture cannot do that.

misconceptions.myth: A 33B model means a 33 GB download.
misconceptions.reality: The original upload is 66237954048 bytes (61.69 GiB) and the Q4_K_M GGUF is 20788825216 bytes (19.36 GiB); the name counts parameters, and the file size depends on how many bits each weight stored in (claims 5 and 6).

misconceptions.myth: Trending on Hugging Face means it is the best open model right now.
misconceptions.reality: It sits fourth on the trendingScore-sorted list with 2,787 downloads while Qwen3.8-27B, on the same list, shows 7,608,285 downloads; trending measures attention this hour, not fit or quality (claim 4).

misconceptions.myth: You can use the whole 512K context on your own machine.
misconceptions.reality: An FP16 KV cache at 512K needs about 104 GiB for the cache alone, before the roughly 19.36 GiB of Q4 weights (claim 7).
No page fetched this run measures what Q4 costs this model in quality; the fit analysis simply treats 4-bit as the only way a 24 GB GPU runs it at all (claims 5 and 8).

glossary.definition: Storing each model weight in fewer bits so the file shrinks; Q4_K_M is a 4-bit llama.cpp format that trades some precision for roughly a third of the original size.
The single-file format that llama.cpp-based tools such as LM Studio and Ollama load.
The working memory a model keeps of the conversation so far, which grows as the context grows.
A model where every parameter fires on every token, like this one, rather than a mixture-of-experts model that routes each token to a subset of itself.
How much conversation the model can hold at once, measured in tokens.
The usual speed measure for local generation: how many tokens of text the model writes each second.

unverified: No page fetched this run reports tokens per second for Nanbeige4.3-33B on named hardware, so every speed claim in the video must be hedged or dropped.
The quality cost of Q4 for this specific model is unmeasured on every page fetched; do not assert that 4-bit is lossless or that it ruins the model.

A reddit thread on r/LocalLLaMA compares AD-IQ4_XS (20.3 GB) and Q4_K_M (20.1 GB) by KL divergence, but reddit returned HTTP 403 to every fetch attempt, so those numbers were seen only in a search snippet.
The Nanbeige4.3-3B student model is named on the card only as a future plan, and no fetched page shows it released.
The AD custom-imatrix quants in AtomicChat's repo were seen only in search snippets, so their quality claims are untested here.
Whether llama.cpp reliably parses this model's XML tool calls is unconfirmed; the webdiga analysis explicitly flags it as not verified.
suggested_outline:
A 33B model sits fourth on Hugging Face trending two days after release, and the question is not whether it is good but whether it fits the RAM you already own.
What it is: a dense Llama-architecture 33B from the Nanbeige team, apache-2.0, billed as the teacher model for smaller 4.3 models, claiming up to 524,288 tokens (512K) of context.
The card's own scores against Qwen3.8-27B: it reports 80.9 to 73.0 on Terminal-Bench 2.12, loses SWE-Bench Pro3 60.3 to 61.7, and trails Gemma4-31B's 91.3 on GPQA Diamond.
The first bill is the download: 66237954048 bytes (61.69 GiB) in BF16, 20788825216 bytes (19.36 GiB) as Q4_K_M.
The second bill is the KV cache: 26.0 GiB at 128K context in FP16, about 104 GiB at the full 512K, all on top of the weights.
The verdict by machine: a 24 GB GPU runs it only as 4-bit with roughly 8K-16K tokens of context, and bigger memory banks buy bigger context.
Tonight: pull the Q4_K_M GGUF into LM Studio or Ollama via the hf.co reference, because no official Ollama tag exists yet.
The honest catch: the scores are the vendor's own, the conversions are day-one community work, and nobody has published tokens per second with hardware.
notes: Two Hugging Face endpoints disagreed on likes within the same morning: the model API showed 512, the trending API 513 minutes later, while both agreed on 2,787 downloads; the radar seed's 508 likes is superseded by these fetched values. A second Q4_K_M conversion (CVLTAI) lands at 20051495648 bytes (18.67 GiB), close to bartowski's, so the roughly-20 GB figure is corroborated across repos; the brief cites bartowski's as the claim source. The card's sidebar already lists 56 community quantization repos and 6 finetunes. Community reception is taken from the repo's own discussion tab (20 threads, including Please release fp8, Which sizes are planned? and It's good, but too slow. Next step, quantize it into three values and put it into 8GB of VRAM.); reddit blocked every fetch with HTTP 403. The webdiga fit analysis states plainly We haven't run it ourselves: its verdicts rest on config math and real file sizes, which is why its claims carry medium confidence.
viewer_situation: You have a gaming PC or a Mac with a fixed amount of RAM, you just watched a 33B model climb Hugging Face trending, and you want to know tonight whether the hardware you already own can run it.
process_steps: Check the free memory on the machine you actually own against 19.36 GiB for the Q4_K_M file, plus room for context.
Download Nanbeige_Nanbeige4.3-33B-Q4_K_M.gguf (20788825216 bytes) from bartowski's repo, or let LM Studio fetch it for you.
Load the GGUF in llama.cpp, LM Studio or Ollama via the hf.co reference, because no official nanbeige tag for 4.3 exists yet.
Set the context length to what the leftover memory can hold, and watch that headroom shrink as the conversation grows.
objection: Every score on the card is Nanbeige's own report, the GGUFs are day-one community conversions, and Qwen3.8-27B on the same trending list shows 7,608,285 downloads to this model's 2,787, so why is this one worth my disk space?
